topics.topic: Cardinality of error entries when several fields have the same error kind
questions: When one input or record has several failing fields of the same error kind, must the answer contain one entry for the input or record, or one entry for each failing field?
When one input or record has failures in two fields of the same error kind, is the answer one entry for the record, one entry per failing field, or one entry containing several fields?
When several fields of one input or record fail with the same error kind, is there one entry for that input or record, or one entry for each failing field?

quotes:
An operation that checks stages (3) to (6) of A04 rule 6 checks
  them in that order and answers the first failing stage with every failure
  of that stage (A04 rule 6): its kinds in the order the operation's Errors
  list them, one entry for each failing input or record, each naming the
  field or the identity it concerns; within one kind, entries are ordered
  first by the record or input they concern — inputs in the order the
  operation's Inputs list them, then records list by list in that same
  order, each list in its own order (A06) — and then, within one record or
  input, by its fields in the order its Inputs or model lists them.

Nothing when every present value is within its form; otherwise every value
outside it, each with its field and its kind: `outside_form` for an alias
over the imported `ALIAS_MAX_CHARACTERS` constant, counted in Unicode code
points, a floor area not greater than the imported
`OBJECT_FLOOR_AREA_MIN_EXCLUSIVE` constant, a number of rooms that is not a
whole number of at least the imported `OBJECT_ROOMS_MIN` constant, a floor
that is not a whole number;
`outside_closed_list` for a kind or language outside its enumeration.

The transaction; the request id; display name, alias, customer reference,
object — address, kind, characteristics; the action's instant.
judgement.divergence: One implementation emits one `outside_form` entry for the failing project input containing both fields; another emits two `outside_form` entries, one for floor area and one for number of rooms. The owner interface and callers inspecting the refusal notice its different cardinality and shape.
judgement.why: The one-entry-per-input clause conflicts in application with the per-field output and field-order clauses without specifying whether multiple same-kind field failures are grouped.

witness.initial: A valid owner session has a project-create form whose required values are present, with floor area 0 and number of rooms 0.
events: The owner browser submits the project create.
`given_values.check_value_forms` finds both values outside their forms and the stage-(4) refusal is assembled.
outcomes: The refusal contains one `outside_form` entry for the project input, grouping the two failing fields.
The refusal contains two `outside_form` entries for that input, one for floor area and one for number of rooms.
witness.observer: The owner browser receiving the rendered refusal.
basis:
`module:operations`. Run one owner request: sign-in and sign-out, the
confirmation step, the upload and the mapping, and every owner action in
its one transaction with its entry and confirmation id (A04, A13, A14, A16).
`module:projects`. Create a project with a request id (A01, R0-44, R0-45).

Nothing when every present value is within its form; otherwise every value
outside it, each with its field and its kind: `outside_form` for an alias
over the imported `ALIAS_MAX_CHARACTERS` constant, counted in Unicode code
points, a floor area not greater than the imported
`OBJECT_FLOOR_AREA_MIN_EXCLUSIVE` constant, a number of rooms that is not a
whole number of at least the imported `OBJECT_ROOMS_MIN` constant, a floor
that is not a whole number;

One HTML page: the answer rendered, every stored value escaped as text for
its place, under a content security policy forbidding any script; or the
refusal rendered — the sign-in page for a request without a valid session.

topics.topic: Ordering of failures across multiple or nested record lists
questions: What declared order determines the order of multiple record lists when records from more than one list have failures of the same kind?
When records are in nested lists, such as each imported project's rooms and pointers, is ordering parent-major or list-kind-major, and what exact sequence of lists does “that same order” denote?
What determines the order between two or more record lists whose failures have the same kind?

quotes:
within one kind, entries are ordered
  first by the record or input they concern — inputs in the order the
  operation's Inputs list them, then records list by list in that same
  order, each list in its own order (A06) — and then, within one record or
  input, by its fields in the order its Inputs or model lists them.

At `mapping`, the mapping: the picked projects by `project_id`, each one's rooms —
`room_id`, name, added instant — and pointers — every fact 'list artifacts'
answers for a pointer but its publisher, which will be the import — in
their lists' orders, the name and alias each arrives under, the
Customers it will make by their v1 value with the projects each links, every
malformed record of the picks, every id of a record the picks bring in that
production already holds — no other production id — and every missing
value; and whether the mapping is clean — no malformed record, no conflict,
no missing value, no given value outside its form or its enumeration —
a name, an alias, a Customer's kind — and at least one pick — which alone lets the confirmation
step be shown.

A collection inside an answer follows the order of the list that answers it
alone: a project card's rooms as 'list rooms'; the agent projection's
pointers as 'list artifacts'; a session's granted ids by `project_id`; the
import mapping's projects by `project_id`, each one's rooms and pointers as
their lists, and the Customers it makes by their v1 value.
judgement.divergence: One implementation traverses each project and reports that project's malformed rooms and pointers before moving to the next project; another reports malformed rooms of all projects before malformed pointers of all projects. The owner interface and ordered-output tests observe the sequence.
judgement.why: Neither “list by list in that same order” nor the mapping's nested collection order selects parent-major versus list-kind-major traversal for failure entries drawn from several nested lists.

The entries are list-kind-major: project 1 room, project 2 room, project 1 pointer, project 2 pointer.

topics.topic: Event and clock sample that determine when a blocked pass can run again
questions: What event fixes “the reading when the pass can run again”: the instant the host resumes or the previous call finishes, the scheduler's first actual execution afterward, or a scheduled deadline; and may an already-due deadline run late if the reading occurs just after it?
Is “the reading when the pass can run again” a monotonic sample taken when the blocking call completes or the host resumes, or the scheduler's next actual clock sample after that event?

quotes:
`instance_lifecycle` makes each of its two passes every
  interval from the start, as A13 rule 2 says of the session pass: the n-th
  call is due when `clock.monotonic_reading` shows n intervals since serving
  began, the first one interval after; a call due while the previous call of
  the same pass is still running is not made, and the pass waits for the
  next due one; deadlines that pass during a suspension of the host or a
  long call are not made up — the next call is the first deadline at or
  after the reading when the pass can run again; a deadline equal to that
  reading is made.

In order: `configuration.load_configuration`;
`backups.probe_backup_location`; `store.open_store`; the owner interface's
listener and then, unless the start is owner-only, the service API's, at
the imported `OWNER_INTERFACE_LISTEN_ADDRESS` and
`SERVICE_API_LISTEN_ADDRESS` constants; then the surfaces answer; then two
passes: `owner_sessions.end_expired_sessions` every imported
`SESSION_PASS_SECONDS` and, except in an owner-only start,
`backups.run_daily_backup_if_due` every imported `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS`, each
from the start as Conventions, "Passes", says.

Due at the first look at or after 03:00 UTC, by `clock.recorded_now`, of a
date an earlier look of this process saw before 03:00, when this process
did not run it, no run is going and no kept backup of the date exists; a
run's date remembered, failed included (A18 rule 1); runs never overlap; the
unencrypted copy removed before the check; a kept name never overwritten;
only files under the two prefixes touched (rule 5); step 3 whatever step 2
did, one cutoff, in name order (rule 4). Never in an owner-only start (rule
9).
judgement.divergence: One scheduler fixes the recovery reading at the instant the host resumes or the prior call completes and executes the first deadline at or after that reading even if its next clock sample is later; another fixes it at the scheduler's next actual monotonic sample and skips every earlier deadline. The owner can observe a due backup starting one interval earlier or later.
judgement.why: The text requires a reading when the pass can run again but does not identify which runtime event takes that reading when readiness and actual scheduling differ.

witness.initial: A token-enabled instance begins serving at 02:58:00 UTC with a 60-second backup-look interval, and the first look at 02:59:00 records that the date is before 03:00.
events: The host is suspended before the 03:00 deadline.
The host resumes immediately before the monotonic reading reaches the 03:00 deadline.
Scheduling delay prevents the pass from sampling the monotonic clock until just after that deadline.
outcomes: Readiness at resume fixes the recovery reading before the deadline, so the 03:00 look runs late and starts the due backup.
The scheduler's actual sample fixes the recovery reading after the deadline, so the 03:00 look is skipped and the due backup starts at the 03:01 look.
witness.observer: The owner interface, which can show the newest kept backup's instant, and a timer test double.

goes on starts none (A18 rules 1, 4, 5; Conventions, "Passes").

topics.topic: Precedence and flattening rules for input and model field ordering
questions: For a value represented both by an operation input structure and by a model, which declaration supplies the field order when their orders differ, and how are embedded model fields flattened?
When a failing value is both an operation input and a model-shaped record, or contains a nested model, which field order takes precedence and how are nested fields flattened?

quotes:
within one kind, entries are ordered
  first by the record or input they concern — inputs in the order the
  operation's Inputs list them, then records list by list in that same
  order, each list in its own order (A06) — and then, within one record or
  input, by its fields in the order its Inputs or model lists them.

The transaction; the request id; display name, alias, customer reference,
object — address, kind, characteristics; the action's instant.
- its object, embedded, exactly one (R0-38, M02);

Facts: address (required at creation, R0-45); kind, one of a closed vocabulary
the specification declares ("Declared vocabularies"), optional at creation; the
declared characteristics, each optional at creation and in every correction:

- its floor area, in square metres, greater than zero;
- its number of rooms as the object has them, a whole number of at least 1 —
  a fact of the object, not a count of the project's Rooms (M03), which are
  the rooms the work names;
- its floor, a whole number, negative below ground and 0 for the ground floor.

Every record the mapping names — malformed or conflicting —
is named by its kind, its id as the file gives it (or that it has none) and
its position among the file's records of that kind, so two records of one
id, and a record with no id, are told apart; a malformed record carries
every rule 4 defect it has, and an id that occurs twice names every record
that carries it.
judgement.divergence: One implementation recursively emits an embedded object's failing fields at the object's position in the Project model; another orders all direct Project fields first and appends embedded-object failures afterward. A caller receiving a malformed imported project with both an object-field defect and a later Project-field defect observes a different defect order.
judgement.why: The convention selects an Inputs or model field order but does not define precedence when both describe the value or where an embedded model's fields enter the containing model's order.

Direct-fields-first flattening reports the status defect before the embedded floor-area defect.
witness.observer: The owner browser and any caller or test comparing the malformed record's ordered defects.

answers for a pointer but its publisher, which will be the import — in
their lists' orders, the name and alias each arrives under, the
Customers it will make by their v1 value with the projects each links, every
malformed record of the picks, every id of a record the picks bring in that
production already holds — no other production id — and every missing
value;

Every record the mapping names — malformed or conflicting —
is named by its kind, its id as the file gives it (or that it has none) and
its position among the file's records of that kind, so two records of one
id, and a record with no id, are told apart; a malformed record carries
every rule 4 defect it has, and an id that occurs twice names every record
that carries it.

One HTML page: the answer rendered, every stored value escaped as text for
its place, under a content security policy forbidding any script; or the
refusal rendered — the sign-in page for a request without a valid session.
